subject: Pricing exhibit: SKU-to-silo mapping and floor/ceiling redlines
messages:
From: Evan Li <evan.li@nimbuslabs.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Novak <rachel@nimblabs.com>, Tom Hsieh <thsieh@nimblabs.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit: initial redline

Hi Avery —

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached is our legal team’s redline to the pricing exhibit. Two items where we need a concrete answer before we can move forward with signature:

1) SKU-to-silo mapping: Our procurement team wants SKU buckets mapped explicitly to deployment silos (hosted / dedicated / private) so that the price bands follow where the workload runs. Can you confirm Redwood can enforce per-silo unit pricing and provide a table?

2) Floor/ceiling guardrails: We pushed back on a hard floor tied to annualized usage because it creates risk for us in year 1. We proposed a seasonality carveout and a 60-day true-up window. Is that acceptable?

We’ve attached the redline PDF (Nimbus-Exhibit-Pricing-Redline.pdf) and a provisional SKU mapping spreadsheet (SOW_Sku_Map.xlsx). Apologies if some of this overlaps with commercial notes — wanted to get counsel in the loop.

Would appreciate a short reply with whether Redwood is willing to commit to per-silo pricing and a proposed true-up mechanism.

Best,
Evan
Evan Li
Head of Procurement, Nimbus Labs
Office: (415) 555-0132

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Evan Li <evan.li@nimbuslabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit: initial redline

Evan —

Thanks for sending the redline and the SKU mapping. Quick update from our side:

- We can support per-silo pricing in the exhibit via an explicit "silo price table" that maps SKU bands to hosted/dedicated/private columns. That will also let us preserve model/version equivalence across silos. I’ve asked Dylan to verify any engineering limits on enforcement (e.g., routed requests that cross silos).

- On floors/ceilings, commercial is open to a seasonality carveout but legal needs to sign off on the language. Karthik — can you review Evan’s proposed 60-day true-up and add suggested language for a carveout tied to documented seasonal events?

Proposed next steps:
- Karthik to circulate a tracked-change version by EOD today.
- Marissa to confirm that commercial can accept per-silo columns and any impact to list prices.
- Evan/Rachel to confirm whether the 60-day window aligns with your billing cycles.

I’m available for a 20-min touchbase this afternoon if that helps.

Thanks —
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0199

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit: initial redline

Avery/Team —

Attached are Redwood Legal’s suggested edits (see Redwood-comments-ExhibitB-track.pdf). High level notes:

1) Per-silo pricing table: We are comfortable including a matrix with explicit columns for hosted/dedicated/private and SKU bands as long as we include:
   - an explicit precedence clause that silo-specific pricing controls only for requests routed to that silo;
   - an operational exhibit that describes how Redwood will determine the request’s silo (region + routing policy + customer pinning) to avoid disputes over billing source.

2) Floors & seasonality carveout: We propose keeping a soft minimum (an annualized floor used solely for quota and true-up calculations) rather than a firm dollar floor that triggers termination rights. Legal prefers:
   - a 90-day true-up window (vs your 60 days) to account for cross-month billing cycles;
   - a defined list of "seasonal events" (e.g., regulatory pilot, initial go-live ramp, marketing promotions) that are excluded subject to Customer notice and reasonable documentation;
   - a mutual review clause for the first 12 months to revisit floor calculation mechanics.

3) Clarifying SKU mappings: The SOW table needs an "effective mapping date" and a change management path for when the customer requests reclassification of a SKU. We added suggested language to require mutual written approval for any SKU re-mapping that changes billable rates.

I left inline comments about indemnity scope tied to dedicated/private deployments (minor tweaks). If commercial is comfortable with the 90-day window, we can push this back to Nimbus counsel for confirmation.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Evan Li <evan.li@nimbuslabs.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Novak <rachel@nimblabs.com>, Tom Hsieh <thsieh@nimblabs.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit: initial redline

Avery / Karthik —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the proposed language. A couple quick points from Nimbus legal:

- 90 days is acceptable but we need an explicit clause that ties the true-up to our standard billing cycle (Nimbus’ invoices are issued on the 1st of the month; we can provide statements to match).
- On the seasonal events list, can Redwood include "product pilot with <30% baseline usage" as an example? Our launch plan will have a multi-week pilot and we want it carved out.
- SKU re-mapping: we accept mutual written approval. One ask: allow our procurement lead (Rachel Novak) to trigger an expedited review process with a 10-business-day turnaround for urgent reclass requests.

We’ve attached a narrow technical change to the SKU map in SOW_Sku_Map.xlsx that clarifies bundle SKUs.

If you can accept the three items above, we should be able to return an executed exhibit next week.

Best,
Evan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Evan Li <evan.li@nimbuslabs.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit: initial redline

Evan / Team —

Appreciate the clarity — commercial signs off on the approach with the following confirmations:

- We will publish a "silo price table" in Exhibit B that shows SKU bands across hosted/dedicated/private. List prices in the table are placeholders until the SOW is finalized; final per-silo prices will be locked at signing.
- Redwood accepts the 90-day true-up window and the linkage to Nimbus’ billing cycle (invoices on the 1st). We’ll include the mutual 12-month review clause.
- We’ll add the explicit seasonal carveout language and include "product pilot <30% baseline usage" as an example.
- For expedited SKU re-maps, Redwood agrees to a 10-business-day turnaround once Rachel triggers the expedited review; if we can’t reach agreement, the prior classification stays in effect until mutual resolution.

Action items:
- Karthik to send final tracked changes incorporating these points on Monday.
- Avery to coordinate with Nimbus for signature timeline; Evan/Rachel to confirm final SOW_Sku_Map.xlsx updates.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the line.

Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0177

(Attachments referenced: Nimbus-Exhibit-Pricing-Redline.pdf, Redwood-comments-ExhibitB-track.pdf, SOW_Sku_Map.xlsx)
